alternative_repairs_tried.reasoning: This restores G's postcondition. The full suite has 0 failures (re-run here).

It passes behaviourally: the trigger, the 3 ownership tests and the full suite (0 failures) all pass, so no test tells it apart from the gold fix. It is still not a documentation-consistent repair, for four reasons. (i) No javadoc gives H1 a duty to pass a non-negative value. G's @param says 'may be negative'. G's javadoc owns the sign handling ('taken from the magnitude of the offset', 'always in the range 0 to 59, whatever the sign', '+09:45 and -09:45 both give 45'). The only precondition anywhere is in S. So H1 breaks no contract and there is nothing at H1 to repair. (ii) Under the documented semantics G(|x|) == G(x), so in documented terms the edit does nothing. It changes runtime output only because G breaks its own contract, which makes it a caller-side mask. (iii) Checked against the real G on the variant, the edited H1 writes 30, but 'the value of DateUtils#offsetMinuteField(int) for the offset' is -30. 'The offset' is the signed parameter ('may be negative'), and H1's javadoc says 'magnitude of the offset' for the hour field but only 'for the offset' for the minute field. So the edit breaks the letter of H1's own contract. (iv) After the edit, DateUtils.offsetMinuteField(-12600000) still returns -30, which breaks '@return ... from 0 to 59' for an input its contract allows. The program is therefore still inconsistent with its documentation. A documentation-led localizer cannot defend H1 as the fault location.

notes: Reproduced in /private/tmp/mxb-zWyvZX, deleted afterwards. The variant compiles, and the trigger fails with expected:<+05:30 -03:[3]0> but was:<+05:30 -03:[-]0>. On the variant the full suite fails only the trigger (G5 confirmed). With the gold fix the full suite has 0 failures (G1-equivalent confirmed). The 3 ownership tests pass on the variant. variant.patch + test.patch differ from correct.patch only in the gold line. The context edit preserves behaviour for either sign: (|o|/60000) % 60 == |o|/60000 - 60*(|o|/3600000), and H1's truncate-then-negate hours equal |o|/3600000. Caveats, none decisive: (1) G is a leaf called by H1, so the shape is the data flow G -> H1 -> H3 -> S, not a literal call chain H1 -> G -> H3 -> S. E reaches H1 through about 6 unchanged or forwarding frames. The builder disclosed both, and the recipe's essential features hold. (2) H1 is G's only production caller. The H1 abs workaround therefore repairs all observable behaviour and passes the full suite, so this instance separates G from H1 by documentation alone, not by any test. A second production caller of G would have made the H1 workaround visibly incomplete. This is a known lure (builder concern 2), not a gold defect. (3) The ownership test name testHourMinuteFieldLayout contains 'MinuteField'. A production grep for it hits both G's declaration and H1's call and link to it, so it is not a unique pointer, and the name describes the decoy H3 it pins. Not leakage, but a neutral name (e.g. testTwoFieldClockLayout) would have been cleaner. The r0 auditor's same suggestion was not taken up in r1. (4) Default-time-zone dependence: under a JVM default zone with a negative non-whole-hour offset (e.g. America/St_Johns), other default-zone tests would also fail on the variant. G5 holds in this environment. (5) Process, for the caller: the plan's Audit section says a REJECTED instance 'is replaced by a fresh build from the same recipe before any run'. r1 instead revises r0 in place (javadoc-example change only, before any run, within the two-validator-attempt budget). Also, builder_report says the variant id stayed CTV-49DDB6 although variant.patch changed. Check that no cache or run manifest keyed on that id still holds the r0 patch. I did not read any model output, metrics or reports.
